content: 1. Triclabendazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of lansoprazole by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzyme CYP2C19. Caution and monitoring are advised. If elevated plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are observed during triclabendazole administration, recheck these levels after discontinuation of triclabendazole. 2. Lansoprazole reduces the plasma concentration or effect of vismodegib by altering its solubility due to increased gastric pH, which may reduce its bioavailability. The impact on efficacy is unknown. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Lansoprazole increases the levels of theophylline by decreasing its metabolism. Prolonged use of proton pump inhibitors can cause hypochlorhydria, which may alter gastrointestinal motility. Monitor for toxicity. 55. Lansoprazole reduces the levels of thyroid desiccated by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding this interaction. 56. Voriconazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of lansoprazole by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Lansoprazole reduces the plasma concentration or effect of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as acalabrutinib solubility decreases with increasing gastric pH. Dose separation may not eliminate the interaction due to the long-lasting effect of PPIs. 58. Apalutamide decreases the plasma concentration or effect of lansoprazole by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzymes CYP2C19 and CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if co-administration is necessary. Adjust the dose as needed. 59. Lansoprazole decreases the plasma concentration or effect of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. If co-administration is necessary, limit the PPI dose to a level comparable to omeprazole 20 mg and administer ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients. 60. Lansoprazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of atogepant by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 61. Lansoprazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of avapritinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 62. Lansoprazole increases the plasma concentration or effect of axitinib by inhibiting the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor closely. 63. Lansoprazole decreases the plasma concentration or effect of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with proton pump inhibitors. 64. Lansoprazole decreases the effects of bosutinib by reducing its concentration by approximately 45%, as bosutinib displays pH-dependent solubility. Monitor closely. 65. Lansoprazole decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent.
